Hi Dana — thanks for the clear asks. I pulled together high-level answers and a proposed cooperation draft to start. Short summary up front:

- Notification: Redwood commits to initial customer notification within 72 hours of confirming a security incident that materially affects customer data; full incident report and remediation summary within 30 days, with updates on a cadence agreed for major investigations.
- Evidence: We can provide SOC 2 incident logs (within 5 business days of a formal request), exported audit trails and relevant KV cache logs (typically 7–14 business days depending on scope), and archived forensic snapshots under joint-scope requests (timeline variable; usually 30–45 days).

I attached a draft of DPA incident cooperation language and an SCCs-focused checklist. Please confirm if Acme needs accelerated SLAs (e.g., 48-hour initial notice) or a narrower evidence window — that would likely need an SLA exception or a committed support package.

I'm looping in Lauren (Legal Operations) and Aditya (Customer Success for Acme) to align on what we can commit contractually vs. what should be operational scope.

Soojin / Aditya — quick legal ops input below. I kept this practical so we can give Acme something to sign.

Proposed clause (short form) to include in DPA:
"Redwood Inference will notify the Customer without undue delay and, where feasible, within seventy-two (72) hours after confirming a security incident materially affecting Customer Data. Redwood will provide a written incident summary within thirty (30) days and reasonable updates thereafter. For incidents impacting cross-border transfers governed by the Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs), Redwood will cooperate to the extent required by applicable law and will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide additional information needed for Customer to comply with SCCs obligations (e.g., scope of data processed, subprocessor list, incident logs)."

Evidence & delivery SLA (operational exhibit):
- SOC 2 incident summary export: within 5 business days of a formal evidence request (redacted where necessary for other customers).
- Audit/trace exports (filtered logs): 7–14 business days depending on time window and retention policies.
- Forensic disk snapshots or raw server images: available only upon joint preservation request and typically require a written mutual scope; delivery timeframe 30–45 business days. Delivery of raw images may be subject to legal process where applicable.

Notes:
- We should add an optional "accelerated response" addendum for customers that require 48-hour initial notice / shorter evidence SLAs — that becomes a paid SLA.
- We need Aditya to confirm operational feasibility and any technical gating (e.g., minimum retention windows for relevant logs).

If that looks OK I'll clean it up and send back to Dana.
